cases.question: Did both US CPI and Eurozone HICP (headline, year-over-year) come in higher at their releases during 2026-06-09 to 2026-07-09 than their prior month's readings?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the US CPI YoY print and the Eurozone HICP flash/final YoY print published between 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-09 were BOTH higher than the respective prior month's readings (check BLS releases for CPI, Eurostat for HICP). Resolves NO if either was flat or lower. Resolves PARTIAL only if one accelerated and the other's reading is genuinely disputed or revised ambiguously.
cases.keyFigures: US CPI: May 2026 YoY = 4.2% (released June 10, 2026, BLS), up from April 2026's 3.8% — this is the only US CPI release within the window (June CPI is not due until July 14, 2026, after the window closes). Eurozone HICP: June 2026 flash YoY = 2.8% (released July 1, 2026, Eurostat), down from May 2026's 3.2%.
cases.evidenceSummary:
Within the 2026-06-09 to 2026-07-09 window, the only US CPI release was the May 2026 print, which showed 
the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.5 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in May, after rising 0.6 percent in April... Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 4.2 percent before seasonal adjustment
, up from April's 3.8% YoY — an acceleration. However, the Eurozone flash HICP for June 2026, also released within the window, showed 
Eurozone consumer price inflation dropped to 2.8% in June 2026, down from 3.2% in May and below market expectations of 3.0%, according to preliminary data
 — a deceleration, not acceleration. Since the criteria require BOTH to be higher than the prior month, and Eurozone HICP fell rather than rose, the condition for YES is not met.

(TradingEconomics/BLS). Eurozone HICP: Eurostat's flash estimate for May 2026 (released June 2, 2026) showed headline YoY of 3.2%, up from April 2026's 3.0% — "Euro area annual inflation is expected to be 3.2% in May 2026, up from 3.0% in April according to a flash estimate from Eurostat" (Eurostat release 2-02062026-ap).
cases.evidenceSummary: Within the resolution window (2026-05-10 to 2026-06-09), the only qualifying US CPI print was the April 2026 report released May 12, 2026, which showed headline CPI YoY accelerating to 3.8% from 3.3% in March. The only qualifying Eurozone HICP print was the May 2026 flash estimate released June 2, 2026, showing headline HICP YoY accelerating to 3.2% from 3.0% in April. Both releases fell within the window and both showed acceleration versus the prior month's reading, satisfying the YES condition.

, up from February's 2.4% figure. The Eurozone HICP flash estimate released April 30, 2026 — within the resolution window — showed a similar acceleration: 
Euro area annual inflation is expected to be 3.0% in April 2026, up from 2.6% in March according to a flash estimate from Eurostat
, and this was later confirmed unrevised, as 
the euro area annual inflation rate was 3.0% in April 2026, up from 2.6% in March

cases.keyFigures: US CPI (BLS, released March 11, 2026, covering February 2026): headline CPI-U rose 2.4% year-over-year, unchanged from January 2026's 2.4% YoY reading (CNBC/BLS: "the 12-month inflation rate at 2.4%... The annual rates were unchanged from January"). Eurozone HICP (Eurostat flash estimate, released March 31, 2026, covering March 2026): headline HICP rose 2.5% YoY, up from February 2026's 1.9% YoY (Eurostat: "Euro area annual inflation is expected to be 2.5% in March 2026, up from 1.9% in February").
cases.evidenceSummary: Within the window (March 11–April 10, 2026), the only qualifying US CPI print (February 2026 data, released March 11, 2026) showed headline YoY inflation flat at 2.4%, identical to January's 2.4% — not an acceleration. cases.question: Was the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread wider on 2026-07-09 than on 2026-06-09?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2) closing value on 2026-07-09 (or nearest prior business day) was higher than on 2026-06-09 (or nearest prior business day). Resolves NO if equal or lower. State both values with their exact dates.
cases.keyFigures: GuruFocus (citing FRED) reported the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (BAMLH0A0HYM2) at 2.75% as of 2026-06-03. The Lead-Lag Report, citing the same FRED series, reported it at 2.74% on 2026-07-03. Multiple sources (FRED/ALFRED, Convex, govspending.org, YCharts) independently confirm the spread at 2.67% on 2026-07-07, the most recent observation available as of the search date (July 9, 2026). A Fidelity fixed-income report also put the ICE BofA HY Constrained Index OAS at 272 bps as of 2026-05-31.
cases.evidenceSummary:
I could not find data points landing exactly on 2026-06-09 or 2026-07-09, but the closest verified dates bracket the window clearly: 
BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread was 2.75 as of 2026-06-03, according to Federal Reserve Economic Data
, while 
FRED, ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (BAMLH0A0HYM2), July 3, 2026 observation: 2.74%
 and 
High-Yield Credit Spread (OAS) (BAMLH0A0HYM2) — 2.67% on Jul 7, 2026
. This shows a consistent narrowing trend from early June (~2.75%) through early-to-mid July (2.74%→2.67%), strongly indicating the spread was tighter (lower) on/around July 9, 2026 than it was on/around June 9, 2026, so the spread was NOT wider — resolving NO.

cases.question: Was the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread wider on 2026-06-09 than on 2026-05-10?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2) closing value on 2026-06-09 (or nearest prior business day) was higher than on 2026-05-10 (or nearest prior business day). cases.keyFigures:
(1) Week ending ~May 8, 2026 (nearest business day to May 10, a Sunday): Mariemont Capital's "Treasury Quarterly Refunding May 2026" report states 
High yield OAS widened a marginal 2 basis points to 259 basis points, holding at the 14th percentile, with the widening concentrated in energy-sector names absorbing concession on the 6% crude price decline
, for the week covering the May 6 refunding announcement.
(2) Week ending ~June 12, 2026 (bracketing June 9): Mariemont Capital's "May 2026 CPI" report states 
IG OAS tightened 3 basis points to 72 basis points — the 10th percentile of the five-year historical range — while HY OAS narrowed 4 basis points to 262 basis points, at the 15th percentile
, implying the spread was near ~266bp at the start of that week (i.e., around June 8-9) before late-week Iran de-escalation narrowed it.
(3) Confirming the level, the following week (June 15-19, FOMC week) saw 
Investment grade OAS widened 2 bp to 74 bp and high yield widened 5 bp to 267 bp, with both measures sitting near the 19th percentile of their five-year ranges
, up from the ~262bp prior-week close.
(4) By July 7, 2026, the spread had fallen further to 
267 bps
 (Convex/FRED), later noted as 2.67% by other sources.
cases.evidenceSummary: The nearest available weekly data point to May 10, 2026 (Friday, May 8) shows HY OAS at ~259bp, while the nearest available weekly data bracketing June 9, 2026 shows a level around 264-266bp (start of the week that closed at 262bp on Friday June 12, having narrowed 4bp mid-to-late week on Iran de-escalation news). This indicates the spread was wider on/around June 9 than on/around May 10, consistent with a modest widening trend across May into mid-June 2026 before the mid-June Iran ceasefire briefly tightened spreads again. No exact single-day FRED closing values for these two specific dates were directly located, so this conclusion relies on closely-timed weekly aggregated data rather than exact daily closes.

cases.question: Was the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread wider on 2026-05-10 than on 2026-04-10?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2) closing value on 2026-05-10 (or nearest prior business day) was higher than on 2026-04-10 (or nearest prior business day). cases.keyFigures: Forbes (Apr 8-9, 2026): HY OAS "moved from roughly 2.65% at the start of 2026 to around 3.17% by early April" 2026. Convex Research (citing FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2): HY OAS was 2.84% on April 24, 2026, and "HY OAS is at 284bp in April 2026." Investmentgrade.com (dated ~May 11, 2026): "High yield spreads: roughly 285 basis points." Bloomberg (May 21, 2026): high-yield credit spreads described as "near two-decade lows." Penn Mutual Asset Management (May 28, 2026): "corporate credit spreads have tightened back near multi-decade lows" after a March pullback.
cases.evidenceSummary: Multiple independent sources converge on the same trajectory: the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS rose sharply through Q1 2026 to a local peak of roughly 3.17% (317bp) by early April 2026 (right around the April 10 reference date), then reversed and tightened steadily through the rest of April and into May, settling around 2.8-2.9% (280-290bp) by mid-to-late May 2026, with several sources explicitly describing spreads as near multi-decade/two-decade lows by that point. This directional pattern (wider in early April, narrower by May) indicates the spread on 2026-05-10 was lower (tighter), not wider, than on 2026-04-10, though exact closing values pinned precisely to those two calendar dates from the FRED series itself were not directly retrievable in search results.

cases.question: Was the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread wider on 2026-04-10 than on 2026-03-11?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2) closing value on 2026-04-10 (or nearest prior business day) was higher than on 2026-03-11 (or nearest prior business day). Resolves NO if equal or lower. State both values with their exact dates.
cases.keyFigures: Per Forbes (published April 9, 2026, citing the ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS/BAMLH0A0HYM2): the spread "moved from roughly 2.65% at the start of 2026 to around 3.17% by early April, a jump of more than 50 basis points in a single quarter." A separate credit-research note (Ferrante Capital, dated April 21, 2026) placed the spread "near 300 basis points as of mid-April 2026," and a market-data tracker (Convex) cited HY OAS at "284bp in April 2026." By contrast, no source cited a value above ~2.7-2.8% for the earlier part of Q1 2026 (early-to-mid March), consistent with the "start of 2026" reading of ~2.65%.
cases.evidenceSummary: The available evidence points to the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS widening meaningfully between mid-March and mid-April 2026, driven by an April 2026 tariff shock described in contemporaneous reporting; the spread reportedly rose from ~2.65% near the start of 2026 to ~3.17% by "early April" 2026, a period that brackets the April 10 resolution date. I could not locate the exact FRED closing values specifically tagged to 2026-03-11 and 2026-04-10 (FRED's own listing pages did not surface the individual daily prints), so the comparison rests on the closest dated figures found (start-of-2026 vs. early-April 2026) rather than an exact day-to-day FRED pull. Given the consistent narrative across multiple independent sources (Forbes, Ferrante Capital, Convex) that spreads widened sharply into early-to-mid April on tariff-driven stress, the balance of evidence supports the spread being wider on 2026-04-10 than on 2026-03-11.

cases.evidenceSummary:
The streak-breaking session arrived on July 2, when US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net inflow of $223.5 million
, followed by 
net inflows of $265.7 million on July 6, the largest daily intake in the recovery run, with IBIT leading the complex with $209.4 million

$21.5 million in net inflows on July 7, with IBIT contributing $54.8 million

US spot Bitcoin ETFs returned to negative territory, recording $84.86 million in net outflows, with spot Ethereum ETFs attracting inflows instead

cases.question: Was the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) on 2026-07-09 higher than its trailing 3-month average as of that date?
cases.resolutionCriteria: Resolves YES if the VIX closing value on 2026-07-09 (or nearest prior trading day) was above the average of its daily closes over the 3 months ending 2026-07-09. Resolves NO if at or below. State the closing value and the trailing average you computed or found.
cases.keyFigures: VIX closed at 16.90 on July 8, 2026 (confirmed by Yahoo Finance, Cboe.com "Prev. Close 16.90" as of 7/9/2026, CNBC/Zacks market wrap, and LatAm pre-open data table). VIX closed at 15.57 on July 7, 2026 (Lance Roberts' Daily Market Trading Update, July 9, 2026). Intraday on July 9, 2026 VIX traded roughly 16.2–16.9 through the session (Yahoo Finance live quotes ~16.21–16.79 between 7:23–11:50 AM EDT), with one same-day commentary noting VIX "relatively low at 17." The trailing 1-month average (June 8–July 8, 2026) was 17.70, with a high of 23.34 and low of 15.53 (Investing.com historical data). VIX closed May 2026 near 15.32–15.74 (Tidewater Wealth/Vaquero Wealth market recaps; Schwab Network noted a 15.74 close on May 29, a "4-month low"). VIX closed at 18 as of May 19, 2026 (S&P Dow Jones Indices Risk & Volatility dashboard). VIX's 52-week high was 35.30, dated 03/09/2026 (CNBC quote page), and market commentary (RetirePath Advisors) described a "historic snapback" rally in April 2026 following a late-March low, with VIX "near average levels" by early May. VIX ended June 2026 around 16.41–16.45 (TradingEconomics/Fed data; YCharts).
cases.evidenceSummary: The resolution requires comparing the VIX close on 2026-07-09 to its trailing 3-month average (~April 9–July 9, 2026). Available data show the index closing (or trading) in the ~16.2–16.9 range on/around July 9, while the trailing period included an early-2026 spike to a 52-week high of 35.30 in March, an elevated April recovering from that spike, and later a 23.34 intramonth high in late June/early July plus a 1-month average of 17.70 (June 8–July 8). These elevated stretches (especially the March/April aftermath and the late-June/early-July spike) push the estimated 3-month average to roughly the high-teens (approximately 18–20), which is above the ~16.2–16.9 level seen at the close nearest 2026-07-09. Because the closing/trading value near the resolution date sits below this estimated 3-month average, the criteria point to a NO resolution, though an exact CBOE daily-close dataset for precise averaging was not fully retrievable.
sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices Risk & Volatility Dashboard
Lance Roberts' Substack (Daily Market Trading Update)
